taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.note: By eye from the photos (observations 328863686, 328863685, 119740253, 322187012, 328863688, 400045236, 154588978, 44034826): a dense tuft of fine, rolled blades and slender culms with narrow, nodding, purplish tan panicles, each spikelet trailing three long spreading awns. The panicle's colour comes from flower_colour through the family's rule, its spikelets from the order's.

traits.life_span.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: perennial, often in large tufts.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: culms 30 to 50 cm tall; FEIS (Howard 1997): a mid-grass with 6- to 12-inch (15-30.5 cm) culms.

traits.culm_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: culms 30 to 50 cm tall; FEIS: 15-30.5 cm culms.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: FEIS species review, Aristida purpurea: a warm-season, native perennial bunchgrass.

traits.clonal.note: FEIS species review, Aristida purpurea: a perennial bunchgrass.

traits.rosette.note: FEIS species review, Aristida purpurea: leaves primarily grow in basal tufts, but there are a few culm leaves.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: blades usually involute and less than 10 cm long; 3 cm to 10 cm drawn.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: blades 1 to 1.5 mm wide when unrolled.

traits.inflorescence.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: panicle narrow, nodding, rather lax and loose.

traits.inflorescence_posture.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: panicle narrow, nodding.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: panicle usually purplish, 10 to 20 cm long.

traits.florets_per_spikelet.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: one floret to a spikelet, as in every Aristida.

traits.glumes.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: first glume 6 to 8 mm long, the second about twice as long.

traits.spikelet_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: the second glume about twice as long as the 6-8 mm first, so the spikelet about 12-16 mm without its awns.

traits.lower_glume_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: first glume 6 to 8 mm long.

traits.upper_glume_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: the second glume about twice as long as the first.

traits.lemma_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: lemma about 1 cm long.

traits.awns.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: awns nearly equal, spreading, 3 to 5 cm long.

traits.awn_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: awns nearly equal, spreading, 3 to 5 cm long; FEIS: 1 to 5 inches (2.5-13 cm) across the species' varieties.

traits.awn_insertion.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 452, Aristida purpurea: the lemma's body tapering to a scarcely beaked summit, the three awns from it.

traits.fruit_type.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: a grain (caryopsis), as in every grass.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: flowering May to September, with the spring and the monsoon rains.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: grains ripe June to October.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for purple threeawn from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.45 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m), batch s1b (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles, Hitchcock and Flora of North America, counts and colours from photos.
